existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Prove that a saturated header (n+1 square-zero units on n fields with product -I) is the image of the sphere-braid relation on a chain of transvections, that Hurwitz moves act on it linearly through the Burau representation at t=-1, and classify its Hurwitz orbits in a fixed integral frame (complete invariant: the mod-2 multiset of the unit vectors; |Sp_n(F_2)|/(n+1)! orbits); prove the arc law for site masks; check the statements exactly on chain-nested roots and the root of #6726.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a source-bound construction. This package is a structure theorem with exact witnesses on literal roots; it constructs no new word, prices nothing and claims no kappa.
bottleneck_link: docs/research/research-family-status.md; the classification states which rewrites of a saturated header are available inside a fixed field frame, which any complete-invoice search over roots has to respect.
stop_rule: No kappa claim. Every statement carries its hypotheses (q^2 = 1, E(q) = 0, ordinary controls absorbed, D = 1, exactly n+1 units, integral frame); applying any of it to a word still needs that word's complete invoice and the five framework assumptions of the cited words.
evidence: PROOF.md (statements and proofs), verify.py (exact checks with negative controls on canonical headers, chain-nested roots and the root of #6726), retained/SOURCE-PINS.json (input pin).

open_questions.question: Can the level-2 step (the pure braid group maps onto Sp_n(Z)[2]) be replaced by a self-contained proof for the header lattice, so that Theorem 4 no longer cites it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Theorem 4 (complete invariant, orbit count) uses the cited theorem; the exact checks cover n = 2 and 4 only.
open_questions.first_step: For n = 6, write each square of a transvection T_v^2 (v a chain vector and v = d_i + d_{i+2}) as an explicit word in the g_i by Euclid-type reduction in the header lattice, and check it exactly.
open_questions.blocked_by: A reduction algorithm for Sp_6(Z)[2] in the generators g_i; the orbit of size 7!*2^21/2 at modulus 4 is too large to enumerate.

open_questions.question: Does the path theorem have an analogue for a central q of order 3, or for non-central controls, and what replaces the value -1?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The path value t = -1 is proved only for q^2 = 1; a different value would change which words can host a pair.
open_questions.first_step: Repeat the telescoping of Lemma 3.1 over F[q]/(q^3-1) with three sector components and compute the rank identity for the resulting unit word on n = 2.
open_questions.blocked_by: The rank identity of #6832 is for an involution; a statement for an order-3 target has to be proved first.

open_questions.question: How do the two moved positions of a Hurwitz move constrain the site masks when masks are defined by commuting idempotents in constant bases?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The package proves that only two units change; whether the moved sites keep a constant-basis mask of bounded size decides which orbit members could be built.
open_questions.first_step: For every single move of chain (3|3) in the frame S_8, compute the smallest idempotents with P x = x, y P = y, [P, U] = 0 for the moved units and compare their ranks with the old ranks.
open_questions.blocked_by: The exact site framework (one variable per site, constant bases) of the pending words has to be fixed in a statement before the comparison is meaningful.

open_questions.question: What are the correct thin queries of the chain-nested family for shapes (even|odd)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The closed form of the cited file gives a non-sign-Gram header for those shapes (checked at (2|1), (2|3), (4|1)); the shapes would be needed for any claim about all chains of one n.
open_questions.first_step: Solve linearly for two thin units with the sign Gram against the left and right queries at (2|1), then generalise the pattern.
